headline: Cedarwave (existing customer): card programme closing, cards will stop; customer's real need is credit — retention risk

suggested_routes.label: Customer follow-up
suggested_routes.rationale: An existing customer must migrate before their current cards stop, and has stated that prepaid-only is their main issue.
suggested_routes.output: Retention follow-up (owner: Team member A for the eligibility check, turn 23). (1) Confirm whether Cedarwave's already-issued bank credit cards can join the transaction feed (turn 23). (2) Confirm accounting-sync feasibility for those bank-card transactions (turn 21). (3) Send a migration plan: old programme closing "in the coming weeks" (turn 4), re-verification of identity for users (turn 6), new account set up in parallel. (4) Book the department/user clean-up session offered in turn 31. The customer will decide internally (turn 29).

suggested_routes.label: Internal / product / vendor note
suggested_routes.rationale: Product and programme questions that the account owner could not answer on the call.
suggested_routes.output: Programme-team questions: are already-issued bank cards eligible for the transaction feed (turn 23)? Can source-balance reconciliation work for bank-card transactions (turn 21)? The available credit limit will not be visible for bank-issued cards (turn 25). Product signal: the customer wants credit, not indefinite prepaid (turns 9, 11), the same theme as M03 turn 6.

suggested_routes.label: Human review
suggested_routes.rationale: A separate 'Migration discussion' meeting with Cedarwave (M13) has no notetaker; it may be related, but only the title suggests so.
suggested_routes.output: Possible association, not confirmed: M13 "SpendNest <> Cedarwave Distribution - Migration discussion" is organised by the same organiser 30 minutes earlier, with no transcript. Confirm whether it is the same conversation or a separate one before combining them.

evidence.quote: We have seen acceptance problems with the existing programme and are proposing a move to a different provider and card network.
The plan is to close the old programme in the coming weeks
Users need to complete identity checks again because the provider changes.
The replacement I described is still prepaid.
evidence.supports: No credit product in the replacement.

evidence.quote: moving from prepaid to credit is the main issue for us. At some stage we will have to consider another option for that.
I need the team to confirm feasibility for your bank-card transactions
I cannot confirm the existing-card eligibility on this call.
evidence.supports: Open eligibility question with a stated owner.

evidence.quote: Then what do we gain by adding SpendNest? We can already see transactions in the bank portal.
We are not deciding the whole migration on this call.

concise_output: An existing customer was told its card programme is closing within weeks and all current cards will stop. The customer said its main problem is needing credit rather than prepaid, and may look elsewhere. SpendNest proposed connecting their bank credit cards, but eligibility and accounting sync are unconfirmed. This is the clearest retention risk in the set.
what_established: Programme closure planned "in the coming weeks"; users must redo identity checks; the replacement is prepaid; credit is the customer's main issue; Team member A will check card-feed eligibility and accounting feasibility; the customer will decide internally.
what_not_established: The closure date, whether the customer will churn, credit eligibility, or deal value. The INR 1.3 crore figure is the customer's existing bank credit line (turn 22), not SpendNest revenue.
next_action: Answer eligibility and accounting questions quickly; send a migration plan; schedule the department clean-up session.
uncertainty: Speaker-to-organiser mapping is not supplied; the association with M13 is title-based only.
